answer: A rolling escrow resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a deposit each epoch, with withdrawals unlocked only after several epochs pass. Attackers spinning up clones must freeze capital matching many honest agents, and since the lockout rolls forward each round, escaped funds cannot mirror the pace of new registrations. Agents failing task checks lose part of their escrow, leaving hollow balances that earn nothing. Saffron status markers rank agents by locked duration, so long-term participants gain priority in task allocation, making clone farms unprofitable.
